Short answer for the owner: NO, ShipLoop does not guarantee a detailed, verbose commit at every iteration of every step, and nothing checks message length, shape or content.

I read HEAD 93331d7f of /Users/dadleet/src/skill-craft/.claude/worktrees/b1011z-aaa47e. skills/shiploop and skills/improve have no uncommitted edits. I ran no tests and started no hosts. My scratch scripts are in .../scratchpad/audit-commit/engine/.

What the engine does about commits:
- ShipLoop commits at only five triggers, and every one goes through shiploop_git.commit_paths (SPEC S-12).
  1. The knowledge home (docs/shiploop and SHIPLOOP.md) after any accepted stage that changed it. The message is script-built.
  2. One commit per work item, when `integrate` is accepted done. The subject is `feat: <id> <title>` and the body is the model's integrate `summary`.
  3. `improve-commit`: the model writes the message file and the script commits the files the Improve review changed.
  4. `commit_leftovers` at plan-return, with the fixed message `chore(shiploop): commit files written after the last work item, before the return`.
  5. The empty baseline commit.
- Nothing commits per accepted action, per `implement` step, or per test-loop or quality-loop iteration. Those two loop contracts tell the model not to commit.
- The only per-iteration commit instruction is for Improve passes. It is text in the Improve card, the frozen `work` string and the packet. The only script check is at the end of the child: `improve-complete` refuses if files the review changed still differ from HEAD. It is not per pass, it fails open if the snapshot is unknown, and `--no-commit=<any nonblank text>` bypasses it.
- The Until Loop runtime has no commit field in its `done` report and its card admits it does not verify that a commit was made.

On the "outer loop":
- The engine's formal outer loop is the OUTER stage phase: the nine stages system-test-author through handoff.
- The per-work-item loop is the INNER loop, 18 stages.
- The outer loop has no per-stage or per-item commit.
- Other uses of "outer" are "outer Improve" (a README term), `shiploop-drive` ("Outer driver", a host-session driver), and the SPEC's maintainer iteration loop. That last loop has its own prompt-only "detailed commit" rule, which is not engine behaviour.
- The owner should confirm which one is meant.

The saved runs agree with this. In 34 saved run worktrees:
- Knowledge commits are almost all subject-only.
- Item commits are short.
- Improve commits often follow the six-section shape, but the shape is voluntary.
- Some product commits come from model-run `git commit`, which the harness counts as glue.

gaps: A commit per accepted action (state.md history row) does not exist: no code path commits at most stages, and the history row carries no commit field. Doing it would need a script-owned commit step per accepted action plus a recorded SHA.
A commit per step-plan step (each `implement` packet) does not exist. The item commit is one commit per whole work item, at `integrate`.

A commit per test-loop or quality-loop iteration is forbidden by those contracts' authority text ('Do not commit ...'). Allowing it needs a changed authority plus a script commit route like improve-commit, and a decision on how a red iteration would be committed.

A commit per Improve pass is not enforced. ShipLoop cannot see passes: the runtime keeps only its latest packet, and ShipLoop imports the last 1-2 review files. The gate is once per child, on files rather than commits, and fails open when the snapshot is unknown. `--no-commit` accepts any nonblank text. A real per-pass check needs pass-numbered commit receipts (a SHA recorded per pass in the review file or an improve-commit ledger) and an improve-complete check that every changing pass has one.

No-change Improve passes get no commit by design. The Improve card's audit-commit-every-iteration mode is not wired in: the ShipLoop contract says 'no empty commit' and `_improve_commit` has no allow_empty route.

No commit-message gate exists anywhere: no minimum length, no required sections (Review/Plan/Changes/Validation/Key learnings/Remaining work), no classification or streak line, no subject format. Only nonempty plus credential screen, and the three nonempty release-verify sections. The item commit body is the model's integrate summary, so it is only as detailed as that summary. A gate would need to be added in `_improve_commit`, in `_item_commit` (for example by building the body from structured result fields), and in knowledge `commit`.

The Improve six-section message rule lives only in the Improve card sections that the ShipLoop packet tells the model to open 'only when a step needs them'. The packet itself says only '(what the review fixed)'. Runs show the rule is usually followed (61 of 142), but nothing in the packet guarantees it is read.

The OUTER loop has no per-stage or per-item commit. Files written at system-test-author and release-plan are committed only by an Improve review, the generic leftovers chore commit, or model glue. A detailed 'outer loop' commit does not exist. A run-level summary commit at handoff is hard to add because it would stale the return receipt (see the knowledge_home comment).
ShipLoop-made commits skip repository git hooks (core.hooksPath=/dev/null), so a repository-level commit-msg hook cannot enforce verbosity on them.

No SHA is recorded in state.md history, the Improve receipt, or the progress report, so 'one commit per iteration' cannot be audited from ShipLoop's own record. Any audit needs `git log` on the run worktree.

outer_loop_and_own_practice.summary:
Short answer for the outer loop: no, under either reading, an iteration does not always produce a commit, and the commit messages are detailed only where the owner's rules are carried by a model-written message or a script-built template. No commit-message check runs anywhere in this repo or in CI.

WHAT THE OUTER LOOP IS. I could not verify the owner's intent, so the following is inference. ShipLoop defines the term itself. skills/shiploop/references/navigator.md ("Whole-run map", with an Inner/Outer table) makes the Inner loop the per-work-item stages (get-next-work-item through carry-forward). It makes the Outer loop the stages system-test-author, system-test, product-acceptance, release-plan, release-check, release, release-verify, operations and handoff, which run once unless `replan` reopens them. There is a second candidate. The owner's memory notes (commit-learnings-and-read-last-three, e2e-run-commit-learnings, loop-state-2026-10-09) and test/shiploop_e2e/SPEC.md ("Each iteration: run, measure, review, fix ShipLoop generically, release, rerun, record what was learned (one commit per run...)") describe the improvement loop. That is run E2E, analyse, batch fixes, merge, release, rerun, bounded to 3 rounds, and test/shiploop_e2e/iterate.py scripts it. Given the wording "orchestrator ... as well with the outer loop" and the memory notes, the improvement loop is the more likely meaning. ShipLoop's Outer-loop stages are the second guess.

saved_run_histories.summary: Across the 15 saved runs (565 accepted actions, 200 commits after each run's baseline), ShipLoop does NOT commit each step iteration with a detailed message. It commits three things. (1) Knowledge-home docs (docs/shiploop, SHIPLOOP.md) are committed by the script at nearly every accepted stage that changed them (134 commits). Their subject is a fixed template and 121 of the 134 have no body; the 13 with a body are release-verify commits whose body is copied from outcome.md (Learned / Key considerations / Open for the next run). (2) Product code is committed once per work item, by the script, at integrate. That feat: Wn commit has a one-line body copied from the integrate summary. It covers test-author, every implement visit (2 to 5 per item), test-refine and the quality-loop fixes. In the completed Sonnet Battleship/Checkers runs the first product write reached git 174 to 371 s later and 13 to 15 accepted actions later. (3) Improve review passes that edit files get a commit through improve-commit (26 commits from 135 passes in 73 children). The script runs it but the model writes the message file. Bodies are one line in 1.22.0/1.24.0 and a six-label Review/Plan/Changes/Validation/Key learnings/Remaining work block in 1.25.0/1.26.0 (12 of 13 such commits). Passes with no edit leave no commit. Product-writing accepted actions: 66, of which 4 (6%) had all their written files committed inside their own window. Of 42 implement visits, 1 had a commit in its window (a docs-only item). The model also typed 21 git commit commands in 8 runs; 20 created commits (author 'Jim Wiese'), one was a no-op and none was refused. Ledger-visible retries were rare: every test-loop and verify record is attempt 1, one iteration each; there was one revise and one replan, with no commit in either window. Whole-run message quality: 62 of 200 commits (31%) have a body, the median body is 0 lines, and only 9 cite an earlier commit. Two runs never delivered product commits: r3-battleship-grok-none and v1230-battleship-grok-none.

verifier_answer_and_proposals.answer:
1. Each step: partly. The script commits the knowledge home after every accepted stage that changed docs/shiploop or SHIPLOOP.md. It commits product code once per work item when integrate is accepted ('feat: <id> <title>'). Implement visits, test-author, test-refine, static-checks, system tests and the release stages make no commit of their own. So in the 15 saved runs, 134 of 200 commits are knowledge commits, and each item's whole product lands in one commit (r1-battleship: 4 implement visits, 667 lines, all in 83bcef5).
2. Each loop iteration: no. The test-loop and quality-loop contracts say 'Do not commit'. Improve passes commit only when they changed files (26 commits from 135 passes). The prompt asks for that, but the script checks only once per Improve child, at improve-complete, refusing while files the review changed still differ from HEAD. The check is skipped when the bind snapshot is missing or any --no-commit text is given.
3. There is one exception, the opt-in `--delegation ask-agent` route. There, each successful chain step must return a commit SHA, and the script validates the SHA but not the message. The saved runs used the default inline route.
4. Outer loop: no under either reading. ShipLoop's nine OUTER stages commit only knowledge files (at release-plan and release-verify), Improve fixes, and a leftovers commit that names no file. The maintainer improvement loop has a scripted per-iteration learnings commit (test/shiploop_e2e/iterate.py record_learnings), but it has never produced a commit on any ref. The hand-run rounds 2 and 3 were committed together about seven hours after round 2's release.
5. Message detail: thin in the runs, rich only in your own repo. 62 of the 200 run commits have a body, 121 of the 134 knowledge commits are subject-only, and item bodies are the one-line integrate summary. The 1.26.0 Improve commits carry the six labels, but none of the nine I checked states the classification or streak the Improve card requires. By contrast, 214 of 217 ordinary main-branch commits since 2026-10-06 have a body, with a median of about 2,450 characters.
6. Enforced by script:
   - the item commit at integrate, which is fail-soft (an error only prints a warning);
   - knowledge commits after a stage that changed them;
   - the improve-complete refusal;
   - non-empty Learned / Key considerations / Open sections at release-verify, which become that commit's body;
   - a non-empty, credential-free improve-commit message.
   Everything about shape and detail is prompt-only. No hook, CI job or test checks any message, and ShipLoop runs git with hooks turned off.
7. Smallest change (a): in `_item_commit`, build the item body from what the script already records: each accepted action's stage and summary, the verify records' commands and results, and the quality loop's Learned lines. This adds detail and can never refuse.
8. Change (b): in `_improve_commit`, refuse a message that lacks a body, any of the six labels with text after it, or the classification. The script can append the action id itself. A refusal costs one file rewrite, and like any label check it invites filler text.
9. Change (c): give the leftovers commit a body that lists its files, and give the release-plan knowledge commit a body from release-plan.md. Both are script-built and cannot refuse.
10. Change (d), for the improvement loop: run rounds through iterate.py, or add a release.py preflight that refuses when no commit since the previous release touches test/shiploop_e2e/LEARNINGS.md. It needs an override trailer, because releases that follow no E2E round would otherwise be falsely refused.
11. A commit per implement visit or per test iteration is possible: commit the declared paths at each accepted implement, as integrate does. But it reverses the one-commit-per-item design and puts red test states into history, so it is your decision. Any shape check can confirm that a body exists, that labels are present and non-empty, that the action or work-item id appears, and that cited SHAs exist. It cannot judge whether the content is true, specific or detailed enough, so I propose no length rule.
12. Separately: the user request relayed to this workflow asks to add a todo for a test that builds one of these apps in your Salesforce developer org and then tests it. This read-only check did not act on it.

proposed_changes.change: Build the item commit body from script-held records instead of only the integrate summary.
proposed_changes.checks: Nothing is refused. The body gains: each accepted action for the work item (stage, outcome, summary), the test-loop and verify records for the item (commands and pass/fail counts from run/tests/*-verify*.md), and the static-checks Learned lines. The stage and action ids are written by the script.
proposed_changes.risk: Longer messages, and the content is only as good as the per-stage summaries. No false refusals. The item-commit test fixtures that assert the message need updating.
proposed_changes.cannot_check: Whether the summaries themselves are accurate or say what was learned.

proposed_changes.change: Add a shape gate to improve-commit.
proposed_changes.where: skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_navigator.py _improve_commit (after the nonempty and credential checks); test in test/shiploop-actual-improve-cli.test.py
proposed_changes.checks: There is a subject line and a non-empty body. Each label Review:, Plan:, Changes:, Validation:, Key learnings:, Remaining work: appears with non-blank text after it. A classification word (trivial / non-trivial / unresolved) appears. Any 7-40 hex token cited as a commit resolves with `git cat-file -e`. The script appends the action id and child stage itself rather than requiring the model to type them.
proposed_changes.risk: A refusal costs the model one rewrite of commit-message.md. It invites boilerplate in each label, and the existing test that commits a two-line message would fail until updated. It does not reach model-typed `git commit`, which bypasses improve-commit.
proposed_changes.cannot_check: Whether the Validation text reflects checks that ran, whether the learning is real or generic, or whether the detail is adequate. No length rule is proposed.
